//: Story Phase 6, chapter 29: The Burning Warning. Night again, everyone below in the sleeping quarters; the captain asleep beside Squawks's basket (Squawks in a tiny sleeping cap: 'Ribbit... taxes...'), Garrick in his enormous hammock in the suit. His stomach turns over and he knows: another major release, bigger than the first. 'Bad noise.' Sharks? Boarders? Fire? 'WORSE.' The evacuation (grab Squawks, get the sleepers moving, up the ladder; 'Pressure shift.' 'It moved.' 'Down.'), the search for somewhere safe on deck (there isn't one), the countdown, and 'Tradition starts somewhere.' Nobody is ever in danger of failing here: it's readable, and it waits.
p6c5.night: The sleeping quarters, after midnight. Gentle chewing at the hull. A groan from the timbers. The coughing bell, now and then, two decks up. Somewhere above, the dead S.E.S. ticks.
Nobody wakes for any of it any more.
You're asleep on the floor by Squawks's basket, one arm round it.
squawks[exhausted]: ...Ribbit... taxes...
captain[tired]: ...Not the frog show... not the frog...

Across the corner, slung from three hooks and a prayer, hangs the biggest hammock aboard. In it, in full suit, sash twisted round to the back, cape draped over the side, medals crooked, snoring like a bilge pump, sleeps the Grand Stenchmaster.
Then, from inside the suit, something shifts.
The snoring stops.
garrick[queasy]: ...Hm.
A warmth. Low down. Spreading. Not the ordinary kind.
garrick[worried]: ...Oh.
A deep, burning pressure, like a kettle somebody has forgotten on the stove for a week.
He knows this feeling. He has felt it exactly once before: on the afternoon the treasure went yellow.
This one is lower. And hotter. And bigger.
garrick[terrified]: Oh, no. No, no, no, no.
squawks[worried]: ...Bad noise.
The hammock swings. Every hook in the room rattles. A tin cup walks off a shelf.
squawks[horrified]: CAPTAIN.
You're awake. So is everyone.
bob[alarmed]: SHARKS?
wick[alarmed]: BOARDERS?
brask[alarmed]: FIRE?
garrick[terrified]: WORSE.
Nobody needs it explained.

p6c5.night.tutorial: Grab Squawks, get the sleepers moving, and get everyone out of the sleeping quarters (the ladder, top right).
p6c5.night.title: The Stenchmaster's About to Blow

p6c5.grab: squawks[horrified]: Not again. Not the cloud. Not the... the feathers... hurt...
He's shaking so hard the little sleeping cap has slipped over one eye.
captain[tender]: Listen to me. Nothing is going to happen to ye this time. Not this time. I promise.
You scoop him up, basket and all, and wrap your coat round the lot.
For once, he isn't performing. His face is grey under the hat.
garrick[worried]: Get him as far from me as you can. The first one nearly killed him.

then.tutorial: Everyone's moving. Up the ladder (top right)!
then.title: The Stenchmaster's About to Blow

p6c5.wake_bob: Barnacle Bob is sitting bolt upright in his hammock, gripping both sides, not moving.
bob[alarmed]: I can't feel my legs, Captain.
p6c5.wake_wick: Wick has pulled the blanket over his head and is reciting the washing schedule.
wick[alarmed]: Tuesday's shirts, Wednesday's socks, Thursday's—
p6c5.wake_brask: Brask is trying to load a pistol in the dark.
captain: Ye'll WHAT? It's a STOMACH!
p6c5.shift: Halfway to the ladder, the Grand Stenchmaster stops dead.
Everyone behind him walks straight into his back.
Panic. Proper panic, the kind with elbows.
p6c5.shift_late: Behind you, the crew come up out of the hatch in a heap, the Grand Stenchmaster last of all. Halfway out, he stops dead, and everyone behind him stops too, mostly on each other.
p6c5.deck: Up on deck, in the dark, the crew pour out of the fore hatch and scatter in every direction, looking for somewhere, anywhere, to be.
There is nowhere on a ship to get away from the thing inside Garrick.
Midships, the Grand Stenchmaster stands very still with his hands on his stomach, as if he's holding a door shut.

p6c5.deck.tutorial: Find somewhere safe to wait it out. (Look around the deck: the main hatch, the rum barrel, the washing line, the rowboat, the rigging, your cabin.)
p6c5.deck.title: The Stenchmaster's About to Blow

p6.refuge.hatch: The main hatch, down to the galley.
hale[alarmed]: Not below, Captain! Below traps it! It'd be the treasure room all over again!
You remember the treasure room. You step back from the hatch.
p6.refuge.barrel: Rook has climbed into the rum barrel and pulled the lid down.
rook: Nobody look at me. I'm a barrel.
captain: Rook. What happens to a smell in a barrel?
The lid comes off rather quickly.
p6.refuge.sail: Sully has wrapped himself in the washing, head first, in about nine shirts.
captain: Ye'll need to BREATHE, Sully.
The shirts come off. He's gone the colour of a plum. He breathes. He wishes he hadn't.
p6.refuge.rowboat: Below it, the sea is solid fins. One of them is looking up at you with real interest.
p6.refuge.rigging: Finch is halfway up the mainmast rigging, going hand over hand toward the crow's nest.
finch[alarmed]: Up's safe, Captain! It can't get UP!
captain: It's a CLOUD, Finch. Clouds go up. That's what they're FOR.
p6.refuge.cabin: Your cabin. Four walls, one door, one little window.
An enclosed room. Like the treasure room was.
p6c5.nowhere: You look over the rail. The sea is fins, fins and more fins, all pointing at the ship.
captain[angry]: GARRICK! Where's it going to GO?
The Grand Stenchmaster points, decisively, at the bow.
Then, equally decisively, at the stern.
garrick[nervous]: ...This office doesn't come with trajectory calculations.
captain[angry]: YOU ARE THE GRAND STENCHMASTER.
garrick[nervous]: The title is MOSTLY ceremonial.
crew: THEN WHY DO WE NEED YOU?
captain: What does 'big one' even MEAN, after the first one?
p6c5.countdown: A long liquid churn, like a bilge pump swallowing a bilge pump.
Thunder, low down, under everyone's boots.
Every medal on the suit rattles at once. The saucepan lid hums.
The seams of the suit creak. The buttons, all mismatched, strain on their threads.
Over the rail, the water begins to froth. Every fin in the sea turns toward the Revenge at the same moment.
garrick[proud]: A Grand Stenchmaster must wear ceremonial attire during a major Stench Event.
The Grand Stenchmaster straightens up, very slowly, like a man listening to something nobody else can hear.
You get down. You wrap Squawks in your coat, and the blankets, and your arms.
garrick[terrified]: THE STENCHMASTER IS ABOUT TO BLOW.
